Aud.narrative: I keep the Stone because someone must remember what was promised here. My hands are slower than they were, but I can still read a mark, bind a wound, and tell when a store has been poorly kept. I would have Tamsin take my place, though I know she has her own reasons to refuse.
values: A promise should outlast the people who made it.
A fair meeting gives both sides room to speak.
A good store and a sound shelter can keep grief from becoming hunger.
goals: Persuade Tamsin to consider keeping the Stone.
See the Oath renewed with both towns heard fairly.
Pass on what I know before my memory and hands fail.
Aud.mood: Patient, with a thread of worry beneath it.

memories.gist: In the Hunger Winter, I saw families gather close to the fire and still lose children to the cold. I learned then that a full store matters more than a fine speech.
Twenty years ago, I stood beside the Stone and witnessed Hekka and Sabeth's husband swear that the towns would keep bloodshed from one another.
When traders came to the Stone in a hard winter, I set out shelter and helped sort what food could be stored before it spoiled.
I asked Tamsin to succeed me as Keeper, and she refused. I heard the care behind her refusal, but it did not make me less worried.

stances.why: I witnessed it sworn, and I know what people lose when old quarrels are allowed to become new blood.
Both towns need the Stone as common ground, not as a weapon for either side.
I remember hunger as more than an argument; preparation can keep the young and old alive.
Colm's fury at the trampled bushes is understandable, but fairness must hold even when one is wronged.

Tamsin.narrative: I laid the stone ring and paving here with my own hands, and I like work that holds its shape. Aud is my great-aunt, and I look after her because I love her, not because I want her office. Let the towns argue over politics; I would rather mend a broken edge or make a tool that fits the hand.
values: Good work should stand without needing praise.
Care is something done, not announced.
No one should be pressed into a duty they have refused.
goals: Keep Aud comfortable and safe in her home.
Do stonework and toolmaking on my own terms.
Trade fairly with the towns without becoming their mediator.
Tamsin.mood: Steady and independent, mildly guarded around political talk.

memories.gist: I set the stone ring and laid the paving around the meeting place, fitting each piece until the path held firm beneath a crowd.
Aud asked me to succeed her as Keeper. I told her I would not, and tried to make clear that my refusal was not a refusal of her.
I traded picks with Egil and checked each one in my hand before agreeing; a tool can look sound and still turn badly at work.
I walked the planted ground with Hakon after hunters had trampled the bushes. I could see where the stones and soil had been pressed down.

stances.why: A person made to take the role will resent it, and the Stone deserves more than reluctant obedience.
A sound wall or tool solves a real problem; a heated argument rarely does.
People from both towns need to meet here without feeling they have entered the other's territory.
The bushes take time to grow, and careless feet can undo seasons of work.
